SCENARIOS
AIM Borg — The Grid (rough draft)
Drag = orbit   Scroll = zoom   Ctrl/Cmd+drag (or Right-drag) = pan
Click a node for its name. Green = AIM App/DB foundation, Cyan = Pipeline, Orange = Waystar calls, Magenta = Rules/Profiles, Blue = destination formats.
Double-click is the universal drill-out trigger everywhere in the Grid; double-click the same node again to close it. Escape steps back one layer at a time.
 • Opening sequence: on load the Grid starts on an empty universe. The AIM EMS Software & Services mark arrives and settles onto the AIM Application node; the AIM Intelligence mark then arrives and settles onto the pipeline anchor, and the model materialises around them. Each mark lands at exactly the size and position of the logo that node already carries, so the intro does not precede the model — it becomes it. AUTOMATED BILLING PIPELINE then forms across the lower frame in the same red as the +EMS in the marks, one letter at a time on a wave running left to right, the line easing its letter-spacing outward as it lands. The copyright and confidentiality line — the same wording as the page header — then rolls up beneath it in white, at about a third the cap height and never at full opacity, so it is legible without competing with the tagline. Last, a biller at work rises into frame to the left — the person the pipeline is built to help, present from the opening frame rather than as an afterthought. The pipeline keeps a biller in the loop by design, and the opening says so before a word is spoken. The sequence then stops and holds all of it on screen indefinitely — that pause is the moment to talk. A key or click releases it: the mark settles onto the pipeline anchor, the model appears, and the Grid hands off with Presentation Mode on and the first Demo Scenario staged at the ePCR node. The Scenarios panel stays shut so the model has the screen to itself; open it from Scen on Borg Control to pick a different scenario. Input during the build-up jumps straight to the hold, so it is never more than two presses from a cold load to a working Grid.
 • AIM Application ball: the AIM Intelligence pipeline sits on top of the core AIM system. AIM Application, AIM Multi-Tenant Database, the customer/agency balls, and the ePCR → ePCR Import Translation chain into AIM Application are all visible from the start — that's core AIM system behavior. Double-click AIM Application to reveal the AIM Intelligence ball (red, with logo); double-click that to reveal the full pipeline. Double-click either again to collapse back.
 • Double-click a fanned-out grid (a "record") to center the camera on it and zoom in close so it's easy to read; double-click it again — or Escape — to zoom back out.
 • Model and SI DB buttons (top-left, under Instructions): two independent on/off toggles for two coexisting layers in the same shared 3D universe, stacked vertically and centered on the same horizontal axis — SI DB on top, Model (the pipeline itself) below. Either or both can be on at once.
 • Model Records button: a second, independent toggle controlling only the currently-open fan-out data cards (not the nodes and pipes themselves, which stay under the Model toggle). Off by default. Every flat node's fan-out (ePCR, AIM Multi-Tenant Database, and the destination nodes) is pre-opened at load, so turning Records on shows real content immediately.
 • On Borg Control specifically: the Model row carries Vis, Rec, SE, ME and Live; the System row carries Pres, SI DB, Fit and Info. Every circle proxies to the corresponding button, so the panel only ever reflects state rather than owning it.
 • Fit button (System row): reframes the camera to a level, front-on view centered on whatever is currently visible — the full pipeline, or just an open fan-out — sized so it fits the window with a little breathing room.
 • Live button (top-left, under Fit): toggles ambient motion on or off. Off by default. Independent of Multiple ePCRs and Single ePCR.
 • Multiple ePCRs button: shows or hides the ambient white flow dots trickling along every pipe at once, representing many claims moving through simultaneously. Off by default.
 • Single ePCR button: a single bright ball travels one complete real path from ePCR to a destination — six payer-resolution routes, Default Profile alone or Default+Selected Profile, and each of the three destination formats (6×2×3 = 36 real paths). Note the format is settled at Payer Selection Rules, not at Bill Payer — a firing rule returns a payer and a form type together — pausing briefly at each destination before the next begins. For a guided walkthrough instead, use Pres.
 • AOH cabinets (Payer/Profile Selection Rules, Default/Selected Profile): these four are drawn as filing cabinets rather than balls, because the hierarchy is what they are. The cabinet front carries the node's name; each of the four drawers is a level, and the level names — System, Organization, Customer, Agency, top to bottom in the order they resolve — are painted on all four sides of the cabinet, so a drawer is identifiable from any viewing angle. Double-click a drawer to fan out that level's rules, double-click again to close; one drawer is open at a time. This replaced an earlier drill-in view that hid the whole pipeline to show the same four levels.
 • ePCR, ePCR Import Translation, AIM Multi-Tenant Database, Patient Account, Eligibility, Insurance Discovery, Claim Scrubbing, 5010/HCFA-1500/Patient Invoice, 837 Batch Claim Submission, 835 Remittance Batch: fan out into their component data grids.
Opening — after the title sequence, a click steps through the big picture: the platform on its own, then the camera pulls back, then the AIM Intelligence layer appears, then the whole model with one slow turn. A further click starts the first Demo Scenario. Press S at any point to skip straight to the scenario.
Layout tuning — Shift+click a node to pick it up. Drag to move it in the plane facing the camera; arrow keys nudge, [ and ] nudge in depth, Shift makes any nudge fine. Enter keeps it and prints the source line to paste back; Esc puts it back where it was. Nothing is saved — a reload returns to whatever the source says.
